curation.why: block is the indented body wrapper — the equivalent of C#'s declaration_list — and anchoring on it adds a level that names nothing. decorated_definition carries a `definition` field, so it looks like a named body to the generator, but it is a wrapper: the function_definition it wraps is the real landmark, and keeping both makes every decorated method a doubled breadcrumb. for_statement and with_statement are control flow that happen to carry a body. expression_statement is any bare expression. A nested function nests statements in real code, so `function` is added as a container even where the generator did not observe a declaration inside one; it is also what makes a closure show up in a trail. Python has no separate `method` node kind — a method is a function_definition inside a class_definition — so `function` covers both and there is deliberately no `method` label here.
